categories.name: Governance & Risk
categories.description: Policies, standards, risk management, compliance, audits, training, roles/responsibilities, exceptions, control ownership.
examples: Security training is completed annually.
Exceptions must be approved and documented.
Risk assessments are conducted annually.

categories.name: Identity & Access Management
categories.description: Provisioning/deprovisioning, authentication, authorization, privileged access, access reviews, MFA, RBAC, SSO, password policies.
examples: MFA is required for administrative access.
Access must be reviewed quarterly.
Privileged accounts require separate credentials.

categories.name: Logging, Monitoring & Detection
categories.description: Logging coverage, log access, retention, alerting, SIEM, monitoring, detection rules, security event review cadence, anomaly detection.
examples: Security logs are retained for 12 months.
Alerts are reviewed daily.
Failed login attempts are logged and alerted.

categories.name: Vulnerability & Patch Management
categories.description: Vulnerability scanning, remediation SLAs, patching, dependency updates, penetration testing, bug bounty, secure configuration baselines.
examples: Critical vulnerabilities are remediated within 30 days.
Penetration tests are conducted annually.
Systems are scanned weekly for vulnerabilities.

categories.name: Secure SDLC & Change Management
categories.description: Code review, CI/CD controls, testing requirements, secrets management, threat modeling, change approvals, release management.
examples: Code changes require peer review before merge.
Secrets must not be committed to source control.
Threat modeling is required for new features.

categories.name: Incident Response
categories.description: Incident detection-to-triage, escalation, communications, customer notifications, postmortems, tabletop exercises, incident documentation.
examples: Incidents must be documented and reviewed post-closure.
Security incidents are triaged within 4 hours.
Tabletop exercises are conducted annually.

categories.name: Data Security & Privacy
categories.description: Data classification, encryption, retention/deletion, data minimization, privacy notices, DSR handling, data access restrictions, key management.
examples: Customer data is encrypted in transit and at rest.
Personal data is retained for no longer than 3 years.
Encryption keys are rotated annually.

categories.name: Third-Party & Vendor Risk
categories.description: Vendor due diligence, security reviews, contractual controls, subprocessors, ongoing monitoring, onboarding/offboarding vendors.
examples: Vendors undergo security review before onboarding.
Subprocessors must meet equivalent security standards.
Vendor access is reviewed annually.

categories.name: Business Continuity & Resilience
categories.description: Backups, recovery testing, RTO/RPO, DR plans, uptime/availability commitments, resilience monitoring.
examples: Backups are tested quarterly.
RTO is 4 hours for critical systems.
DR plan is reviewed and tested annually.

categories.name: Physical & Endpoint Security
categories.description: Device security, MDM, EDR, endpoint hardening, office controls, facility access, asset handling in physical contexts.
examples: Corporate laptops must use full-disk encryption.
Endpoint detection and response is deployed on all devices.
Physical access to server rooms is logged.

categories.name: Customer / Contractual Commitments
categories.description: External promises and contractual obligations: SLAs, audit rights, notification timelines, data use restrictions, reporting commitments.
examples: Customer will be notified within 72 hours of a breach.
Customers may request audit reports annually.
Data is used only for the contracted purpose.

categories.name: Product / Fraud-Specific Controls
categories.description: Product-specific integrity/security controls: model security, fraud/abuse monitoring, decisioning auditability, customer-facing product control promises.
examples: High-risk transactions are subject to enhanced review.
Fraud detection models are audited quarterly.
Decisioning logic is logged for auditability.
